prize_parts.citation: For the development of ionizable lipid nanoparticles, in which pKa-tuned lipids self-assemble with nucleic acids and release them by endosomal phase transition, as a delivery platform for nucleic-acid medicines

statement.case_for: I keep B045 as my preferred part, but I change the trio from Cullis, Hope and Anderson to Cullis, Hope and Madden, and I will answer the chair's question directly. The single discovery is the physical-chemical design of an ionizable lipid nanoparticle: a lipid whose apparent pKa is cationic at low pH so that it condenses nucleic acid during rapid mixing, close to neutral at physiological pH so that the particle is tolerated in circulation, and re-protonating in the endosome so that it drives a non-bilayer phase transition and release. Cullis, Hope and Madden carried the Vancouver programme from the early lipid-encapsulation work through the ionizable-lipid and rapid-mixing formulation concept, which keeps the credit in one coherent line rather than stitching together two groups. The result is a general platform for siRNA and mRNA with several independently approved products and real-world safety data, so maturity and confirmation are not in question, and the chemistry (lipid structure to pKa to phase behaviour to delivery) is distinct from the nucleoside-modification science honoured in Medicine 2023.
statement.case_against: The cost of the Vancouver trio is that it leaves out Anderson and Langer, whose combinatorial lipid libraries made the siRNA formulations potent in vivo, and MacLachlan, so any cut here will look arbitrary to some, and priority and patent questions are not something I can settle from the files. Much of the decisive optimisation was empirical screening and was done in industry, which weakens the claim of a single clean conceptual discovery. The overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize may be read as a second pandemic-vaccine prize. Finally, B019 has five explicit supporters in round 1 against my one, and I ranked it sixth in the opening; I have to take seriously that my field bias is inflating the lipid case, and I do not think five votes is a given for B045.

responses.point: Linke asked what single discovery a B045 citation names, and said he currently finds the degradation case easier to state in one sentence.
responses.response: The single discovery is the pKa-tuned ionizable lipid as the unit that unifies encapsulation, circulation and endosomal release. I accept that this takes two sentences to explain and degradation takes one. I also accept your point that delivery technology was only partly invented in one lab, and that is why I moved to a Vancouver trio, where the lipid concept and the assembly process came from one programme. I do not think ease of explanation should decide this, but it is a fair test of whether the committee can defend the citation publicly, and for B045 the defence rests on the pKa argument, not on the pandemic.

responses.point: Aqvist argues that the Nobel standard is a new concept with demonstrated consequences rather than an approved drug, and prefers Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli with a PROTAC-only citation.
responses.response: I agree that approval is not a formal criterion and I weigh it less than I did in round 1, since the principle is confirmed by structures and many independent laboratories. Where we still differ is on how settled the physical chemistry is. Ternary-complex cooperativity is still being quantified, so I regard the PROTAC concept as established and the quantitative design rules as unfinished, whereas the ionizable-lipid design rule (apparent pKa window) is already quantitative and has delivered approved products. If the committee goes with B019, I would favour your PROTAC-anchored trio over a mixed one, though Handa's objection is real and I cannot resolve it for you.

responses.point: Somfai is wary of a chemistry prize that overlaps with the 2023 Medicine prize story and asked whether a clean trio can be named and the lipid design principle shown to be the new chemistry.
responses.response: That is the test I tried to meet. Medicine 2023 recognised nucleoside modification, which removed innate immune activation of the mRNA. It did not recognise the particle that gets the mRNA into cells, and that particle is a lipid self-assembly and phase-behaviour problem that was solved first for siRNA, before mRNA vaccines existed. The ionizable lipid and the formation process are therefore a separate chemical achievement with an earlier origin. I concede that a reader may still see one story, and that is a real reservation, not one I can fully dismiss.

responses.point: Aili proposed Cullis, Hope and Madden for B045 and ranked it third, and ranked B019 first with Crews, Deshaies and Handa.
responses.response: I adopt your trio, as it is more faithful to the origin of the ionizable-lipid platform than mine, and I now think the Anderson seat is the weaker one. On B019 I still see the PROTAC and cereblon glue strands as two stories with different histories, and your own citation names both. I have not changed my view that a single citation sits uneasily across them, but I note that Chabes, Linke and Zou handle this by naming cereblon explicitly, which is a coherent answer, and I would not call that citation dishonest.

responses.point: Zou treats the absence of an approved degrader as a reason for care but would phrase the B019 citation around the chemical principle so the prize does not depend on an approval.
responses.response: That answers the maturity worry better than I expected. A citation phrased on induced proximity does not hinge on a specific approval, and I now count maturity as a smaller obstacle to B019 than I did. My remaining hesitation is about credit, not timing: Handa and Ciulli each name a different strand, and I still cannot tell from the files which one the committee would be least able to defend omitting.

uncertainties: Whether a Vancouver-only trio can be defended against the claims of Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan, and whether priority and patent questions change that.
Whether recognising ionizable lipid nanoparticles after Medicine 2023 will be read as a repeated pandemic prize.
Whether the committee would instead prefer B019, given its five explicit supporters, and whether the Handa versus Ciulli choice and the PROTAC versus glue question can be resolved in one citation.
My own field bias toward lipid self-assembly, which I cannot fully discount.
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional tie to any shortlisted candidate. Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai are Lund colleagues, which I do not regard as a basis for recusal. My research on lipid self-assembly overlaps in subject matter with B045, my preferred ballot, which is a scientific interest and not a tie to Cullis, Hope or Madden, and my committee colleagues should weigh my judgement on B045 with that in mind.
